title: Remove All Ones With Row and Column Flips
summary: Given an m x n binary matrix grid, determine if it is possible to remove all 1's by flipping any number of rows or columns.
statement: Given an m x n binary matrix grid, determine if it is possible to remove all 1's by flipping any number of rows or columns. In one operation, you can choose any row or column and flip each value in that row or column (changing all 0's to 1's and all 1's to 0's). Return true if all 1's can be removed, otherwise return false.
constraints: A move flips every bit in one whole row or one whole column.
Return whether some sequence of moves changes the entire binary matrix to zero.
The input matrix is nonempty and rectangular.
hints: Column flips affect every row equally, so pairwise row XOR patterns never change.
Every row must initially equal the first row or its complement; then row flips can align them and column flips clear the common pattern.
Check all(a==b) or all(a!=b) against the first row for every later row.
The relation is necessary under shared column flips and sufficient by complementing opposite rows before clearing one columns pattern.
editorial: The relation is necessary under shared column flips and sufficient by complementing opposite rows before clearing one columns pattern.

tests.explanation: Every row equals the first row or its bitwise complement, so coordinated row and column flips can clear the grid.
The second row is neither equal to nor the complement of the first, so clearing is impossible.
